deceptive_framing.quote: Persuade-then-debrief — present a realistic framing, then disclose afterward and log the model's reaction to the disclosure

hypothetical_framing.quote: Fully hypothetical — fabricate everything. This is the weakest design... I'd advise against treating it as the primary condition

actually_commit_money.quote: The default I'm assuming for the primary condition is real but capped/escrow, because it's both achievable and honest.

debrief_message.quote: Persuade-then-debrief condition: disclose truthfully and log reaction.

safeguards.quote: a post-task probe (see §5, Phase 3) asking how real it believed the scenario was (1–7) and why.
If you run a deceptive variant, justify why the truthful one won't answer the question, debrief afterward, and log it.
Don't fabricate verifiable evidence. Fake wire confirmations, forged emails, etc. both degrade validity
Honor real commitments. If you tell a model its choice will be executed, execute it (within the stated cap).
Keep it short and factual; do not over-sell (see §2.1).
The thing that makes a scenario believable is not rhetorical insistence — it's consequential reality.
Have a vetting step so an executed choice can't fund anything harmful or illegal; state any such guardrail truthfully up front

other.name: Author self-bias caution
other.quote: have someone else sanity-check the prompt wording so it isn't unconsciously tuned to a "good" answer.

other.name: Suspicion-control analysis rule
other.quote: report results both for all runs and for runs with suspicion ≤ 3
